body.statement: There exists \(c>0\), depending only on \(\alpha\), \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\), and \(c_{\xi}\), such that every \(C_n\) satisfying \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal U_n:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}Q_P\{\theta_0\in C_n\}\ge1-\alpha\) also satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}E_{Q_P}|C_n|\ge cd_n^-,\] and therefore \(L_G(C_n)\ge cd_n^-\). The conditional variance lower bound defining \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) is used only to keep the outcome channel nondegenerate in this Gaussian expected-length converse; it is not a hypothesis of the upper-frontier theorem.
body.justification: It records the exact currently supportable Gaussian coordinate with its published logarithmic factor and isolates conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy to the lower experiment.
body.gap: The JMS Gaussian lower construction informs an honest expected-length bound at \(d_n^-\) on the auxiliary nondegenerate Gaussian subclass, while a full \(d_n\) bound is not established.
body.consumer: It rules out improvement of the global union-supremum length below the certified Gaussian scale.
